new.why: AWS documented a production evaluation lifecycle that spans development, release, runtime and feedback stages.
new.summary: Agent evaluation combines business facts, task rubrics and layered tool-to-orchestration tests across the deployment lifecycle.
new.why_now: AWS's October 16 case study adds nine named stages, bounded test sets, canaries and drift checks.
new.practical_value: Design one release gate that catches factual, safety, latency and cost failures before broader traffic.

novelty.reason: Nine linked evaluation stages extend familiar model testing into an explicit production agent lifecycle.

evidence.reason: AWS provides named stages, test-set sizes, failure examples and reported outcomes, although some numeric examples are illustrative.

independence.reason: The framework and measurements come from one AWS-authored implementation without independent replication or customer audit.

momentum.reason: This first observation supplies no comparable repeated measure collected under the same evaluation protocol.

relevance.reason: Teams can directly translate business failure modes into merge gates, release thresholds, canaries and drift alerts.

durability.reason: Continuous evaluation across development and runtime addresses a persistent reliability need beyond any single model.

momentum.reason: No two comparable dated numerical observations establish momentum for this framework.

new.why: AWS exposed the serving and hardware decisions required to evaluate a large open-weight coding model.
new.summary: Open-weight coding models require explicit checkpoint, precision, sharding, cache, runtime and hardware choices before evaluation.
new.why_now: AWS's October 16 guide documents Reflection Beam deployments through JumpStart, HyperPod, SGLang and vLLM.
new.practical_value: Compare quality, first-token latency, throughput and cost under the exact configuration expected in production.

novelty.reason: A large open-weight model focused on agentic coding adds a configurable alternative to managed proprietary endpoints.

evidence.reason: AWS documents architecture, checkpoints and multiple deployment paths, but supplies no independent task-quality benchmark in this guide.

independence.reason: Current implementation evidence is entirely AWS and Reflection authored, with no separately operated deployment evaluation reviewed.

momentum.reason: One release guide cannot establish directional change in adoption, performance, operating cost or deployment reliability.

relevance.reason: Engineering teams can reproduce configuration tests and measure quality, latency, throughput and resource requirements before adoption.

durability.reason: Checkpoint portability and transparent serving choices remain useful even as particular runtimes and accelerator generations change.

momentum.reason: No repeated comparable deployment observation supports a numeric momentum score.

new.practical_value: Audit one workflow's data, controls, exceptions and outcome measure before purchasing broader assistant access.

novelty.reason: The topic reframes familiar AI readiness around complete processes rather than counts of deployed assistants or pilots.

evidence.reason: SAP cites Oxford Economics survey findings and explicit percentages, while the underlying questionnaire and sample are not reproduced.

independence.reason: The accessible evidence is vendor-sponsored research presented by SAP without an independent survey replication reviewed here.

momentum.reason: This single survey publication provides no comparable prior observation using the same readiness definition and sample.

relevance.reason: Knowledge-work leaders can test data, ownership, approvals, exceptions and outcomes on one process before scaling spend.

durability.reason: Process integration, governed data and accountable operating change remain durable constraints across changing AI products.

momentum.reason: No comparable longitudinal survey observation is available for momentum scoring.

momentum.reason: The different vendor examples report structures rather than one shared outcome measure, so trend scoring is unsupported.

relevance.reason: Teams can inspect one bounded package, run deterministic fixtures and keep script execution behind an explicit approval.

durability.reason: Focused instructions, lazy context loading and reviewable code boundaries remain useful across agent framework implementations.

momentum.reason: Available implementations do not publish one comparable repeated outcome measure.

updated.why_now: AWS's October 15 framework supplies a dated control model and identifies where proof cannot replace judgment.
updated.practical_value: Classify one task's controls as provable, observable or judgment-based before granting additional tools or access.

novelty.reason: The five-layer model sharpens earlier task safeguards by explicitly separating proof, observation and contextual human judgment.

evidence.reason: AWS provides detailed control definitions and examples, but no independently measured comparison of deployment failure rates.

independence.reason: AWS's governance model is organizationally separate from prior Google physical-control evidence, though neither has external replication.

momentum.reason: Earlier safeguards and this conceptual framework use incompatible measures and cannot support a numeric direction of change.

relevance.reason: Teams can map identities, permissions, tool policies, audit evidence and escalation points onto one bounded agent task.

durability.reason: Scope, least privilege, external enforcement and accountable judgment are durable control needs across model generations.

momentum.reason: Available safeguards lack a shared repeated numerical metric for momentum.
